content.text: Doppelkopf (meaning 'Double Head') is Germany's most widely played trick-taking card game, deeply embedded in German social culture. It is played with 48 cards (double deck of 9-A in 4 suits). Crucially, partnerships are NOT fixed â€” they are determined secretly each hand by who holds the two Queens of Clubs. Players use bidding signals to find their partner. The trump suit is extensive: all Queens, all Jacks, and all Diamonds are permanent trump.

Doppelkopf evolved from Schafkopf in Northern Germany. Its name refers to playing with a 'double head' (double deck). It is referenced as early as the 19th century but became codified in the 20th century through the German Doppelkopf Association.

Doppelkopf is played by exactly four players in the standard game. Two form the Re team and two form Kontra; the partnership is not fixed at the start—it is determined secretly by who holds the Queens of Clubs. With five people present, the game can be played with the dealer sitting out each hand.
48 cards: Double deck of 9-10-J-Q-K-A in 4 suits (9s to Aces); 8s and below discarded. Each rank appears TWICE.
Cards. Score sheet or Ramsch log.
